summary: Trump announces an "economic D-Day" against Iran, imposing unprecedented economic warfare and secondary sanctions on any nation providing Tehran a financial lifeline. The US military has established a controlled shipping lane in the southern Strait of Hormuz, moving 10-20 million barrels of oil daily under American fighter escort. Meanwhile, IDF strikes in Gaza eliminated senior Hamas commanders at a police station in Daraj Tuffah and in Shati camp.

US military creates controlled shipping lane in southern Strait of Hormuz, enabling 10 million barrels/day oil transit, half pre-war volume. (Source: @VahidOnline/77959)

IRGC spokesman claims daily advancements in weapon precision and destructiveness, warning future war would see different arsenal. (Source: @N12chat/222688)

sections.executive_summary: Trump announces an "economic D-Day" against Iran, imposing unprecedented economic warfare and secondary sanctions on any nation providing Tehran a financial lifeline. The US military has established a controlled shipping lane in the southern Strait of Hormuz, moving 10-20 million barrels of oil daily under American fighter escort. Meanwhile, IDF strikes in Gaza eliminated senior Hamas commanders at a police station in Daraj Tuffah and in Shati camp.

points: Trump declares "economic D-Day" on Iran, announcing the toughest economic operation ever against any country: Iran's navy is gone, air force destroyed, military factories ruined, currency worthless, and the state hangs by a thread. He threatens severe economic consequences for any country allowing its financial institutions, businesses, airports, or government entities to provide Iran any lifeline, including oil smuggling, swap lines, cash transfers, exchange houses, ship registries, and shell companies. (Source: @lelotsenzura/94195, @mamlekate/104190, @inon_yttach/9889, @Faytuks_Network/6419)

IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohavi states Iran advances daily in all weapons domains, producing arms that are more precise, more destructive, and more technologically advanced; he warns that if war breaks out again, Iran's arsenal will be fundamentally different from before. (Source: @N12chat/222688)

Satellite imagery confirms an air strike on the Iranian Air Defense Control and Reporting Center (CRC) near Karaj during the 39-day war; the post-strike image is dated June 28, 2026, sourced from GEOIMINT. (Source: @shin_persian/9031)

Trump claims total control of the Strait of Hormuz, saying many ships passed last night and a very large volume of oil is flowing, though the situation is not completely ideal; he notes countries are seeking alternatives like Texas, Alaska, and Louisiana. (Source: @yediotnews25/134115, @rodast_omiddana/79524)

The US military has established a controlled shipping corridor in the southern Strait of Hormuz along the Omani coast, with 15-20 tankers transiting nightly in two convoys, moving roughly 10 million barrels per day (up to 15-20 million on some nights). The operation is coordinated by a special group at Fort Bragg, protected by US fighters against Iranian cruise missiles and drones, and followed a two-week CENTCOM operation that degraded Iranian radar and maritime surveillance. (Source: @VahidOnline/77959)

Iranian attacks on shipping persist: some vessels have been damaged, but US forces intercepted 8 Iranian drones and 2 cruise missiles earlier this week; Iran now relies on a few rebuilt radars and IRGC speedboats for surveillance. (Source: @VahidOnline/77959)
Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf met with the Iraqi Prime Minister in Baghdad. (Source: @rodast_omiddana/79523)

IDF Chief of Staff, visiting Syria, states Israel monitors changes on the Syrian front and will not allow hostile forces to entrench on its borders, vowing to apply military power precisely where and when needed. (Source: @idf_telegram/24933)

IDF and Shin Bet struck a gathering of terrorists at a civilian police station in Daraj Tuffah, northern Gaza; at least four Hamas military wing operatives and one Popular Resistance Committees operative were present, using the facility for terror planning against IDF forces in violation of international law. (Source: @idf_telegram/24935)
Half an hour before the police station strike, the IDF eliminated a Hamas platoon commander who had infiltrated Israel on October 7. (Source: @idf_telegram/24935)
An IDF strike in Shati camp eliminated a Hamas company commander and three Nukhba platoon commanders. (Source: @inon_yttach/9885)
An attack was reported on the Gaza promenade, though details were not specified. (Source: @lelotsenzura/94189)
Gaza Health Ministry reports 10 new martyrs and 25 injuries arrived at hospitals in the past 24 hours. (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/385811)

IDF strikes in Daraj Tuffah and Shati camp targeted Hamas military infrastructure and commanders, including a company commander, three Nukhba platoon commanders, and a platoon commander who participated in the October 7 infiltration. (Source: @idf_telegram/24935, @inon_yttach/9885)
Terrorists operated from a civilian police station to plan attacks against IDF forces, violating international law. (Source: @idf_telegram/24935)
Ongoing Israeli military operations in northern Gaza continue to target Hamas Nukhba forces. (Source: @idf_telegram/24935, @inon_yttach/9885)
IDF Chief of Staff visited Syria, monitored front changes, and warned against hostile force entrenchment near Israeli borders. (Source: @idf_telegram/24933)
Iranian Parliament Speaker Qalibaf met with the Iraqi Prime Minister in Baghdad. (Source: @rodast_omiddana/79523)

The UAE announced suspension of all financial and economic transactions with Iran following US pressure to tighten oversight on IRGC financial networks; the move could significantly reduce Iran's access to foreign currency and global trade networks, though Emirati officials view it as gradual escalation rather than total rupture, seeking to preserve diplomatic channels. (Source: @asafroz/52597)

The US established a controlled shipping lane in the southern Strait of Hormuz, enabling 10-20 million barrels per day of oil flow, escorted by US fighters and coordinated from Fort Bragg. (Source: @VahidOnline/77959)
Trump suggested alternatives to Hormuz oil, citing Texas, Alaska, and Louisiana, stating people are coming to the US for oil. (Source: @rodast_omiddana/79524)

sections.threat_assessment: The simultaneous imposition of maximum economic pressure on Iran and the establishment of a US-controlled oil transit corridor in the Strait of Hormuz indicates a coordinated strategy to strangle Iranian revenue while maintaining global energy flows. Iran's degraded air defenses and maritime surveillance, evidenced by the CRC strike near Karaj and reduced radar coverage, limit its ability to contest the new shipping lane. However, IRGC claims of advancing weapon precision and continued drone/missile attacks on shipping suggest asymmetric retaliation remains likely. Israeli operations in Gaza and Syria demonstrate continued multi-front military pressure on Iranian proxies. The UAE's financial decoupling adds a critical non-military dimension to the pressure campaign.
sections.regional_response: Gulf states are aligning with US pressure: the UAE's suspension of financial ties with Iran marks a significant shift, though Emirati officials frame it as gradual escalation rather than total rupture, reflecting concerns over Dubai's financial hub status and non-oil economic exposure. Iraq hosts Iranian diplomatic engagement (Qalibaf visit) while balancing US influence. Regional actors are hedging: Trump's touting of US oil alternatives (Texas, Alaska) signals a long-term effort to reduce Gulf dependence on Hormuz, but current oil flows through the US-controlled corridor remain vital. No unified Arab stance emerges; each state calibrates its exposure to US secondary sanctions versus Iranian retaliation.
sections.intelligence_notes: The June 28, 2026 satellite imagery of the destroyed Iranian CRC near Karaj confirms Israeli/US strike capability deep inside Iran during the 39-day war, degrading integrated air defense. The US Fort Bragg-coordinated shipping lane operation represents a novel maritime security architecture, bypassing Iranian-controlled northern Hormuz routes. Intelligence on IRGC financial networks in UAE appears actionable, given the rapid Emirati compliance. Hamas's use of civilian police stations for command and control in Gaza persists, providing IDF legal justification for strikes under international law. The reported 10 million barrels/day through the southern corridor is a measurable metric for monitoring the effectiveness of Iran's maritime interdiction attempts.
